page.overview:
What is Bonnie the Rabbit?

Bonnie the Rabbit is one of the animatronics in the Five Nights at Freddy's novel trilogy. He is the guitarist of Freddy Fazbear's Pizza created by Henry Emily. He appears an antagonist and supporting character in the first two novels respectively.

Bonnie's appearance is similar to his game counterpart, being a life-size animatronic rabbit about the size of an adult or taller. His body is segmented like an artist’s model, with each limb made of distinct, squarish pieces, separate at the joints. Bonnie has bright blue fur, a squared-off muzzle with a giant permanent smile, and thick-lidded pink glass eyes that are wide and chipped. He also has long ears, large blue paws, large padded feet, and a wide, square face. Bonnie holds a red bass guitar, and around his neck is a bow tie that matches the instrument’s fiery color. A bolt anchors him to the stage.

In The Twisted Ones, Bonnie appears more withered and dirty, as his blue fur is stained and matted. He still holds a red bass guitar in his hand, though it is battered and broken. Half of Bonnie’s bright red bow tie has torn off, giving his face a lopsided look.

Prior to becoming the bass guitarist at Freddy Fazbear's Pizza, Henry worked on Bonnie and the animatronics at his home, hanging their suits in the attic. One day, he showed three endoskeletons off to his daughter Charlie, who managed to identify each based on the simplest of features. Once the restaurant was opened by Henry and William Afton in Hurricane, Utah, the town came alive. Bonnie was particularly adored by a little girl named Jessica, who found him to have an understanding look and would discuss her problems with him. When five children disappeared at the restaurant in 1985, it was closed down.
